dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3601.text: Long boards for building rammed-earth walls. Formed from 木, with 𢦔 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Chu besieged Cai, marking out a circuit and erecting wall-boards.”

shuowen:3602.text: To pound or ram. Formed from 木, with 筑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3603.text: End-posts for building a rammed-earth wall. Formed from 木, with 倝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3604.text: An end-post, 榦. Formed from 木, with 義 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3605.text: A covering or roof. Formed from 木, with 冓 indicating the sound. Du Lin regards it as the graph for rafters.

shuowen:3606.text: A model or standard. Formed from 木, with 莫 indicating the sound. Read like 嫫 in 嫫母.

shuowen:3607.text: A name for a ridgepole. Formed from 木, with 孚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3608.text: The ridgepole, 極. Formed from 木, with 東 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3609.text: A ridgepole. Formed from 木, with 亟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3610.text: A pillar. Formed from 木, with 主 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3611.text: A pillar. Formed from 木, with 盈 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Paint the pillars of Duke Huan’s temple red.”

shuowen:3612.text: A slanting pillar or brace. Formed from 木, with 堂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3613.text: A pillar base, formerly wood, now stone. Formed from 木, with 耆 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Persisting in deep-rooted constancy brings misfortune.”

shuowen:3614.text: A wall-post capital, 𣝍櫨. Formed from 木, with 咨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3615.text: A wall-post. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 薄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3616.text: A bracket block above a pillar. Formed from 木, with 盧 indicating the sound. Yi Yin says: “Among fine fruits, east of Mount Ji, at Qingfu, are 櫨 oranges, ripe in summer.” Another explanation: the 宅櫨 tree, growing in the Hongnong mountains.

shuowen:3617.text: A roof bracket block. Formed from 木, with 幵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3618.text: A roof support, 栭. Formed from 木, with 𠛱 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Those shrubs and those 栵.”

shuowen:3619.text: The projecting support above a roof’s bracket block. Formed from 木, with 而 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “栭 is called 㮞.”

shuowen:3620.text: A ridge beam, 棼. Formed from 木, with 㥯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3621.text: A rafter. Formed from 木, with 𤋯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3622.text: A rafter; a square rafter is called 桷. Formed from 木, with 角 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Carve the rafters of Duke Huan’s temple.”

shuowen:3623.text: A rafter. Formed from 木, with 彖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3624.text: What Qin calls a roof 椽, Zhou calls 榱 and Qi and Lu call 桷. Formed from 木, with 衰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3625.text: The Qin name for the connected roof-eave timbers; Qi calls them 檐, Chu 梠. Formed from 木, with 眉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3626.text: An eave timber, 楣. Formed from 木, with 呂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3627.text: An eave timber, 梠. Formed from 木, with 𣬉 indicating the sound. Read like 枇 in 枇杷.

shuowen:3628.text: The connected timbers at the roof eaves. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 𨘢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3629.text: An eave timber, 㮰. Formed from 木, with 詹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3630.text: The front of a roof’s eave timber. Formed from 木, with 覃 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a silkworm-raising mallet, 蠶槌; its precise use is uncertain.

shuowen:3631.text: The lintel above a doorway. Formed from 木, with 啻 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “檐 is called 樀.” Read like 滴.

shuowen:3632.text: A doorpost. Formed from 木, with 直 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3633.text: A door pivot. Formed from 木, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3634.text: A door. Formed from 木, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3635.text: A building with an upper story. Formed from 木, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3636.text: The lattice openings of a room. Formed from 木, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3637.text: A railing. Formed from 木, with 盾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3638.text: The small uprights between railing posts. Formed from 木, with 霝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3639.text: A ridge beam. Formed from 木, with 亡 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “杗𢊺 is called 梁.”

shuowen:3640.text: A short rafter. Formed from 木, with 束 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3641.text: A plastering tool; Qin calls it 杇, east of the passes 槾. Formed from 木, with 亏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3642.text: A plastering tool, 杇. Formed from 木, with 曼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3643.text: A door pivot is called 椳. Formed from 木, with 畏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3644.text: The crossbeam holding a door pivot. Formed from 木, with 冒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3645.text: A door peg or threshold. Formed from 木, with 困 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3646.text: A threshold. Formed from 木, with 㞕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3647.text: A wooden barrier. Formed from 木, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3648.text: A prop or support. Formed from 木, with 倉 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 槍 means 欀, a supporting timber.

shuowen:3649.text: To bar a door. Formed from 木, with 建 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3650.text: A wedge. Formed from 木, with 韱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3651.text: A wedge. Formed from 木, with 契 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3652.text: Timbers set together as a fence. Formed from 木 and 冊; 冊 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:3653.text: A fence or enclosure. Formed from 木, with 也 indicating the sound. Read like 他.

shuowen:3654.text: Something struck by those making rounds at night. Formed from 木, with 橐 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Double gates, with clappers struck.”

shuowen:3655.text: A marker at a roadside pavilion or postal station. Formed from 木, with 亘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3656.text: A wooden tent or canopy. Formed from 木, with 屋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3657.text: The central pole of a tent. Formed from 木, with 童 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3658.text: The crosspiece at the front of a bed. Formed from 木, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3659.text: A small table before a bed. Formed from 木, with 呈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3660.text: 桱桯, called 蕩 in the east. Formed from 木, with 坙 indicating the sound. The exact furnishing is uncertain.

shuowen:3661.text: A seat for resting the body. Formed from 木, with 爿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3662.text: What supports the head when lying down. Formed from 木, with 冘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3663.text: 楲窬, a toilet vessel. Formed from 木, with 威 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3664.text: A chest. Formed from 木, with 賣 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a tree name. Also: a large chopping stand, 梡.

shuowen:3665.text: The general name for coarse and fine combs. Formed from 木, with 節 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3666.text: To arrange the hair. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 疏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3667.text: A sword sheath. Formed from 木, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3668.text: A weeding tool. Formed from 木, with 辱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3669.text: A 㭉, a spade. Formed from 木, with 入 pictographic and 䀠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3670.text: A two-edged spade. Formed from 木; 绂 is pictographic. Song and Wei call it 㭉.

shuowen:3671.text: A spade. Formed from 木, with 㠯 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a tool for moving earth, in Qi speech; the wording 纪 is uncertain.

shuowen:3672.text: The end of a plow. Formed from 木, with 台 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3673.text: A six-pronged plow. Another explanation: the curved timber above a plow, its shaft. Formed from 木, with 軍 indicating the sound. Read like 渾 in 渾天.

shuowen:3674.text: A tool for smoothing fields. Formed from 木, with 憂 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “He kept harrowing without stopping.”

shuowen:3675.text: A chopping tool, called 鎡錤 in Qi. Another explanation: an axe handle naturally curved in its grain. Formed from 木, with 屬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3676.text: A chopping tool is called 櫡. Formed from 木, with 箸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3677.text: A wheat-harvesting tool. Formed from 木, with 巴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3678.text: A seed drill. Another explanation: the implement 柃𣒃 used in roasting wheat. Formed from 木, with 役 indicating the sound; the second implement is uncertain.

shuowen:3679.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3680.text: A flail for beating grain. Formed from 木, with 弗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3681.text: A flail, 柫; called 柍 in Huainan. Formed from 木, with 加 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3682.text: A pounding pestle. Formed from 木, with 午 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3683.text: To level the grain in dou and hu measures. Formed from 木, with 旣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3684.text: To level. Formed from 木, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3685.text: Three crossing timbers supporting a cooking basket. Formed from 木, with 省 indicating the sound. Read like 驪駕; the reading instruction is uncertain.

shuowen:3686.text: The Rites mentions 柶; 柶 is a spoon. Formed from 木, with 四 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3687.text: A drinking vessel, 㔶. Formed from 木, with 否 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3688.text: A supporting tray. Formed from 木, with 般 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3689.text: A tray. Formed from 木, with 虒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3690.text: A kind of small table. Formed from 木, with 安 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3691.text: A round table. Formed from 木, with 瞏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3692.text: Defined as 钌, perhaps a container; the recorded gloss is uncertain. Formed from 木, with 咸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3693.text: A ladle. Formed from 木 and 斗.

shuowen:3694.text: A ladle handle. Formed from 木 and 勺.

shuowen:3695.text: A wine vessel with tortoise-eye decoration, carved from wood with cloud-and-thunder patterns, symbolizing inexhaustible giving. Formed from 木, with 畾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3696.text: A round wine container. Formed from 木, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3697.text: A wine vessel. Formed from 木, with 盍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3698.text: An elongated vessel inside a cart’s basket framework. Formed from 木, with 隋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3699.text: Called 槌 east of the passes and 㭙 west of them. Formed from 木, with 追 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3700.text: A mallet. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 特 indicating the sound.
